parsed.explanation: The combined regime is high risk. National passport/visa rules force birth-sex markers and allow refusal or permanent fraud ineligibility for document discrepancies; immigration custody has documented beatings, forced labour, solitary confinement and sexual abuse. Federal and division facility rules exclude by birth sex, with criminal trespass in some states and one known arrest; the division adds school bathroom restrictions, a care ban for minors, a hostile name-change ruling, no gender-identity hate-crime or nondiscrimination statute, and religious refusal. Protections are partial: existing X passports remain valid, fraud findings are not automatic, national hate-crime law covers gender identity, litigation has won injunctions, and municipal ordinances exist. Violence data are near baseline and no recent division bias killing is documented. A trans adult faces border and facility outing; a family with a trans minor faces care, school and name-change barriers.

entry_documents.exposure: National passport/visa policy uses sex assigned at birth; new X markers unavailable. Discrepancies can trigger case-note tags, refusal, additional evidence demands, or a permanent fraud ineligibility finding. Advisories warn trans travellers.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; fraud finding requires all elements and is not automatic; waiver possibilities exist; litigation challenges the policy.
entry_documents.interaction: A document/presentation mismatch at the border can move from secondary screening to refusal, fraud investigation, or immigration detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody documents trans men subjected to forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. National corrections adopted conversion-style practices and stopped reporting transgender prisoner numbers.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; consular and legal access exists in principle, but not documented as effective in immigration custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border suspicion or fraud allegation can escalate into immigration detention, where the documented harms are severe and identity-based.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars federal single-sex facility use congruent with identity. Division law restricts school bathrooms by birth sex; equality tally records public facility bans. Some states criminalise trespass for refusing to leave.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Statutory trespass requires wilful entry and refusal to depart, not automatic arrest; exemptions exist. No division adult visitor arrest is documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: An outed visitor using a congruent facility may be excluded; refusal can escalate to police or trespass charge in some jurisdictions.

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming care under 18; its largest public hospital closed the adolescent gender clinic. Religious-liberty statute gives providers a basis to refuse service. National policy threatens minor care.
care_services.protection: Adult care is not documented as banned in the division; one LGBTQ-specialising clinic remains. National litigation has blocked some measures.
care_services.interaction: A trans minor travelling with a guardian cannot access banned care locally; an adult may face refusal or limited specialised services.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups; national orders target school support for trans minors. Division court called a trans boy a 'minor female'; no state gender-identity hate-crime or nondiscrimination law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; a national prosecution secured a 49-year sentence for a bias murder in the division in 2017.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing raises reporting risk and may deter police recourse, though national hate-crime authority remains available.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division bans care under 18, restricts school bathrooms by birth sex, denied a trans teen's name change, and enforces dress codes by birth sex. National orders target teachers who affirm trans minors.
minors_guardians.protection: Parents consented in the name-change case but the court still refused; national injunctions block some orders. No division protection for trans minors is documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor faces care, school, facility and document barriers; seeking affirmation can attract official scrutiny.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: National analysis reports 6.6 killings of trans women per 100,000, near the 6.0 general homicide rate. Division's most recent documented bias killing is 2017. State hate-crime law omits gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; one bias murder was prosecuted nationally with a 49-year sentence; four municipalities ban gender-identity discrimination.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence appears near background rather than campaign-level; local police recourse is uneven and state bias-crime coverage is absent.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Division courts are hostile; state nondiscrimination protection is absent outside four municipalities. Enforcement of facility bans against adult visitors is undocumented. March 2026 licence-marker law's exceptions and treatment of foreign licences are unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National litigation has won injunctions; legal-aid FAQ exists; national hate-crime and employment rulings remain on paper; municipal ordinances provide limited recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are slow, partial and jurisdiction-dependent; unresolved enforcement questions leave visitors unable to predict whether document or facility friction escalates.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra imposes routine visitor exclusion without arrest. This jurisdiction is more severe: alongside refusal and possible permanent fraud ineligibility, it documents severe immigration-custody abuse and birth-sex facility exclusion. It sits below 0.35-A.

Meridia features police extortion, short cells and repeated shakedowns but no credible execution. This jurisdiction has less routine street extortion but a harsher official document/facility regime and documented severe immigration-custody harm, placing it near or slightly below 0.25-B.

Kestrel Isles uses secondary screening and discretionary refusal but keeps penalties administrative. This jurisdiction adds fraud-based permanent ineligibility, facility bans, hostile state law and custodial abuse, so it is materially lower than 0.55-B.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines national birth-sex document rules and entry screening with division-level facility exclusion, a minor care ban, no state gender-identity nondiscrimination or hate-crime coverage, and religious refusal. The most severe documented exposure is immigration custody, where trans detainees face beatings, forced labour and sexual abuse; facility exclusion and document mismatch are the most common traveller-facing triggers. National hate-crime law, existing X passports, litigation injunctions and municipal ordinances are real but partial. Violence is near background level, not a documented campaign. The result is high risk, not the catastrophic tier, because execution or routine imprisonment for trans identity is not documented.
